title: Peptide Label Roll Core and Outer Diameter: Will the Roll Fit Your Applicator?
seoTitle: Peptide Label Roll Core & Diameter | RP Labels
description: Specify core inner diameter, finished roll outer diameter and liner width before ordering peptide vial labels for a tabletop or automatic applicator.
alt: AI-generated printed RP peptide label roll, sample vials and tabletop applicator with a visible cardboard core
caption: AI-generated packaging illustration, not an RP factory photograph or a measured equipment setup. Confirm core and roll dimensions against your actual applicator manual.
intro: A roll can contain the right label, in the right direction, and still fail before the first vial reaches the applicator.
sources: HERMA: printed roll labels, cores and maximum roll diameter

title: Variable Data on Peptide Vial Labels: Check the Lot Before Releasing the Roll
seoTitle: Peptide Label Variable Data Release | RP Labels
description: Separate preprinted artwork from later lot and date coding, then approve the finished vial label with a documented data and print-quality check.
alt: AI-generated fully printed RP research vial labels with sample SKU names and illustrative lot fields beside a variable-data printer
caption: AI-generated workflow illustration. SAMPLE fields and any code-like marks are decorative examples, not real lots, valid dates, verified barcodes or RP production records.
intro: The artwork proof can be perfect while the variable field on the finished vial is wrong. Those are two different approvals.
sources: GS1: ten steps to barcode your product
GS1: 2D retail implementation and variable-data printing

title: Opaque Supplement Overlabels: Covering Old Artwork Without Creating a New Problem
seoTitle: Opaque Overlabels for Supplement Bottles | RP
description: Before covering outdated supplement packaging, test opacity, fit, adhesion and the entire corrected information panel on the real bottle.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness supplement bottles comparing an old printed label and a proposed opaque correction label
caption: AI-generated correction-label illustration. The bottle copy is fictional and not a compliant supplement label or an approved packaging change.
intro: An opaque sticker is not a time machine. It can hide old ink; it cannot make an unreviewed correction legally or operationally sound.
sources: Avery Dennison: cover-up opaque range and correction-label applications

title: Supplement Labels Scuffed in Shipping: Test the Pack, Not Just the Ink
seoTitle: Supplement Label Shipping Scuff Test | RP
description: Identify abrasion contact points in supplement shipments and compare label finishes with the actual bottle, carton and fulfillment route.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness supplement bottles with one scuffed printed label beside an e-commerce shipping carton
caption: AI-generated packaging illustration, not a measured abrasion test or a claim about RP shipment performance. Decorative bottle copy is fictional.
intro: The bottle looked fine on the packing table. By the time the customer opened the mailer, the front panel looked tired.

title: Holographic QR Labels: Make the Security Design Shine Without Losing the Scan
seoTitle: Holographic QR Label Scan Testing | RP
description: Test QR readability on finished holographic labels by managing reflective areas, opaque code panels, quiet zones and the actual package surface.
alt: AI-generated iridescent RP Secure hologram labels with white QR demonstration panels and a phone camera over a carton
caption: AI-generated concept image. The code-like marks are not functional identifiers and the pictured phone is not an authentication result or verification report.
intro: A hologram is supposed to move in the light. A code is supposed to stay readable in it. Putting both on one tiny sticker is where a good-looking proof can fail.
sources: GS1: 2D barcode retail implementation, reflectance and quiet zones
GS1: 2D barcode colour and reflectance guide
